text:
sara: quick sync — noticed a regression where some client SDKs auto-retry on socket resets during streaming and end up re-sending the request body. observed in a Go integration test: stream got a TCP reset, client retried once and the server processed the prompt twice (side effects). wondering what our official guidance should be for SDKs: when to auto-retry vs when to bubble up the error?

mike: ugh — yeah that can cause duplicate side effects. my gut: automatic retries are OK for idempotent endpoints (embeddings, pure-compute generation without side effects) but we should NOT silently replay request bodies that might be non-idempotent (anything that triggers billing or DB writes). for streams specifically, prefer resume tokens / partial-state resume rather than blind replays.

jin: agree. concrete rules I'd propose: 1) If endpoint supports resume tokens, SDK should try to reconnect and resume using token — do NOT replay original request. 2) If endpoint is inherently idempotent, SDK can retry on network errors and 5xx with exponential backoff + full jitter. 3) For 429: respect Retry-After header if present; if missing, treat like a backoff with longer base and larger jitter window. 4) For non-idempotent endpoints without resume support: expose the transport error to callers and provide helpers to attach idempotency-key headers.

mike: +1. Also add a max total retry budget (e.g., max attempts and max elapsed time) so clients don’t keep spinning forever. for streaming clients, the SDK should default to no auto-retry for connect failures unless user opts in.

jin: here's a tiny Go pseudo-snippet we can include in the SDK guide: ```go // simplified retry loop for non-stream requests const maxAttempts = 5 base := 200 * time.Millisecond for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++ { resp, err := httpClient.Do(req) if err != nil { // network error -> backoff if attempt == maxAttempts { return nil, err } sleep := time.Duration(rand.Int63n(int64(base) << attempt)) time.Sleep(sleep) continue } if resp.StatusCode == 429 { if ra := resp.Header.Get("Retry-After"); ra != "" { dur, _ := time.ParseDuration(ra + "s") time.Sleep(dur) } else { time.Sleep(time.Duration(rand.Int63n(int64(1<<attempt))) * base) } continue } if resp.StatusCode >= 500 { // server error -> backoff and retry continue } return resp, nil } ```

ops-bot: note: linking this thread to the SDK retry-patterns doc card (internal). :link:

mike: small nuance — the snippet is fine but we should distinguish between transport-level failures and application-level 5xx. For transport failures during request body stream (e.g., streaming upload) we must not re-open and resend the body unless the body is replayable (buffered or idempotency token present).

sara: for the PR I’m about to open, I added an option for "AutoRetryPolicies" with three presets: none, conservative (no stream replays, retries only on idempotent endpoints), and aggressive (replay if body is replayable). pinging reviewers @mike and @jin to sanity-check behavior before merge. also: can someone confirm the phrasing for docs: "Clients SHOULD respect Retry-After for 429; otherwise use exponential backoff with full jitter and a capped retry budget" — ok to add?

jin: phrasing looks good. suggest we add a short checklist for language maintainers: 1) document resume-token support, 2) show idempotency-key example, 3) include snippet for Retry-After + backoff, 4) mark default policy = conservative.

mike: approve on the approach. only ask to add an explicit example of how to surface the transport failure to apps (e.g., error type NetworkRetryableError vs ApplicationError) so downstream apps can decide to re-run vs not.

sara: perfect, I’ll update the PR with checklist + error type suggestion. thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created card DEVEX-428 to update language SDK docs and add unit tests for socket-reset cases.

sara: filing a follow-up test task: add an integration test that simulates socket reset mid-stream and asserts no automatic replay unless resume token present. adding it to the PR now.
